pointers.sentence: A class whose body defines no media attribute is given one, a property that `media_property` makes for it, as `Widget.media` is (`django/forms/widgets.py:MediaDefiningClass.__new__`).

Its extend attribute says what of the inherited to keep: all of it by default, none with `extend = False`, only the types a list names with `extend = ("js",)` (`django/forms/widgets.py:media_property`).

A `Media` is made from an inner class's css and js, or from arguments of those names: a dictionary of lists of paths keyed by medium, and a list of script paths (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media.__init__`).

An object with `__html__` is kept as it is: a `Script` or `Stylesheet` written in the declaration, which takes no medium from its key, or a safe string holding a whole element (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media._normalize_js`, `django/forms/widgets.py:Media._normalize_css`).

An object with `__html__` is kept as it is: a `Script` or `Stylesheet` written in the declaration, which takes no medium from its key, or a safe string holding a whole element (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media._normalize_js`, `django/forms/widgets.py:Media._normalize_css`).

A `Media` keeps the declarations it was made from, each apart, and `Media.__add__` makes a new one holding the left's declarations and then each of the right's that is not empty and not equal to one already there (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media.__add__`).

It gives each declaration to `graphlib.TopologicalSorter` as a chain, each asset after the one before, so an asset in two lists is one node, placed after everything any list puts before it (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media.merge`); two assets are one when they share class, path and attributes (`django/forms/widgets.py:MediaAsset.__eq__`).

It gives each declaration to `graphlib.TopologicalSorter` as a chain, each asset after the one before, so an asset in two lists is one node, placed after everything any list puts before it (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media.merge`); two assets are one when they share class, path and attributes (`django/forms/widgets.py:MediaAsset.__eq__`).
A `Media` drawn as a string is `Media.render`: the stylesheets, by medium in alphabetical order, then the scripts, one element to a line, marked safe (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media.render`).

`media["css"]` and `media["js"]` are new `Media` objects holding only the stylesheets or only the scripts, so a template can write `{{ form.media.css }}` in its head and the scripts at its end (`django/forms/widgets.py:Media.__getitem__`).

So `{% csp_nonce_attr form.media %}`, new in 6.1, puts the Content Security Policy nonce, when the context holds one, on every element but those given as safe strings (`django/utils/csp.py:nonce_attr`) ([The built-in tags](../templates/tags.md), [Content Security Policy and the nonce](../security/csp.md)).

Both are `MediaAsset` subclasses, whose property `MediaAsset.path` resolves the path at each drawing: one beginning with `"http://"`, `"https://"` or `"/"` is kept, and any other goes to `static`, which asks the static files' storage for its URL when `django.contrib.staticfiles` is installed and otherwise joins it to `STATIC_URL` (`django/forms/widgets.py:MediaAsset.path`, `django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.handle_simple`).

`BaseForm.media` adds the media of each field's widget, hidden ones too, in the order of the instance's fields, so a widget a form puts in place in its `__init__` counts (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.media`).
`MultiWidget.media` is the sum of its subwidgets' (`django/forms/widgets.py:MultiWidget._get_media`).

A formset class is not made by `MediaDefiningClass`, so an inner `Media` on one is never read (`django/forms/formsets.py:BaseFormSet.media`) ([Formsets: `BaseFormSet` and the management form](formsets.md)).
